related_questions.question: How do I disinfect my house after staph infection?

text_blocks.snippet: To disinfect your house after a staph infection, focus on cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces, washing laundry in hot water, and maintaining good personal hygiene. Bleach solutions (1/4 cup bleach per gallon of water for surfaces with 5.25%-6.0% bleach) or EPA-registered disinfectants can be used.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on cleaning and disinfecting frequently touched surfaces, washing laundry in hot water, and maintaining good personal hygiene

list.snippet: Identify surfaces: Prioritize cleaning and disinfecting surfaces that are frequently touched, like doorknobs, light switches, countertops, and handles.
Prepare a bleach solution: Mix 1/4 cup of bleach with 1 gallon of water, or follow the instructions on your disinfectant's label.
Clean first: Use a detergent or cleaner to remove dirt and grime before disinfecting.
Disinfect: Thoroughly wet the surface with the disinfectant and let it air dry. Do not rinse unless the product label specifies.
Use separate cloths: Avoid using the same cloth for multiple surfaces to prevent cross-contamination.
Wash in hot water: Wash clothing, bedding, and towels in hot water with laundry detergent.
Dry thoroughly: Dry items on the hot setting in the dryer.

Wash hands frequently: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after using the bathroom, before and after preparing food, and after touching potentially contaminated surfaces, according to the MN Dept. of Health.
Avoid sharing: Do not share personal items like towels, razors, and clothing.
Consider professional help: If you have concerns about widespread contamination or have difficulty cleaning certain areas, consider consulting a professional cleaning service, says the CDC.
Follow product instructions: Always read and follow the instructions on any cleaning or disinfecting products you use.
Monitor for recurrence: Be vigilant about any signs of a staph infection returning and seek medical attention if needed, says the CA Department of Developmental Services.

text_blocks.snippet: To clean for a staph infection, focus on hand hygiene, wound care, and disinfecting surfaces. Regularly wash hands with soap and water, keep cuts and scrapes clean and covered, and disinfect surfaces that may be contaminated, especially after contact with infected areas.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on hand hygiene, wound care, and disinfecting surfaces

list.snippet: Wash hands frequently with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, especially after touching potentially contaminated surfaces or before and after touching wounds.
Use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer (at least 60% alcohol) when soap and water are not available.
Clean wounds with soap and water, even if they don't appear infected.
Cover wounds with a clean, dry bandage to prevent the spread of bacteria and keep them from being touched or scratched.
Change the bandage daily and whenever it becomes wet or dirty.
Use a disinfectant on frequently touched surfaces like countertops, door handles, and shared items.
Follow the instructions on the disinfectant label for proper use, including contact time.
Consider using EPA-registered disinfectants that are effective against Staphylococcus aureus or MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus).
Wash clothing, towels, and bedding in hot water and dry them thoroughly in a hot dryer.
Avoid sharing personal items like towels, washcloths, razors, and clothing.
Don't share personal items.
Avoid contact with other people's wounds or bandages.
If you have a staph infection, avoid contact sports and public facilities like gyms and pools until the infection has healed.
Staph bacteria can survive on surfaces for a period of time, so thorough cleaning and disinfecting are crucial.
If you suspect a staph infection, consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.
Some staph infections, like MRSA, may require specific treatment protocols and precautions.
